# Causal-argument check: claim "wearing less in cold/overcast weather (X) causes arthritis (Y)".
# An option undermines the claim most if it shows X present with Y absent in a comparable
# situation (the cause without the effect). Cases of Y without X do not refute X as a cause,
# because arthritis can have several causes.

options = {
    # (cause_present, effect_absent, comparable_context, shows_alt_cause_only)
    "A": dict(X=True,  notY=True,  comparable=False, alt_only=False),  # Japanese women, different context; also garbled "because"
    "B": dict(X=True,  notY=False, comparable=True,  alt_only=False),  # supports X as a trigger
    "C": dict(X=True,  notY=True,  comparable=True,  alt_only=False),  # same city, same habit, no arthritis
    "D": dict(X=False, notY=False, comparable=True,  alt_only=True),   # Y without X: only shows other causes
}

def strength(o):
    s = 0
    if o["X"] and o["notY"]:
        s += 2          # cause without effect: a direct counterexample
    if o["comparable"] and o["X"] and o["notY"]:
        s += 1          # controlled comparison, so other variables are held similar
    if o["alt_only"]:
        s += 0          # does not refute a cause that is sufficient but not necessary
    if o["X"] and not o["notY"]:
        s -= 1          # supports the claim
    return s

scores = {k: strength(v) for k, v in options.items()}
print("scores:", scores)
best = max(scores, key=scores.get)
print("best option by model:", best)
submitted = "D"
print("submitted:", submitted)
if best == submitted:
    print("CHECK PASS")
else:
    print("CHECK FAIL")
